title: Why Trust Your Agent? Empirical Security Gains from TRiSM-Guided Agentic Workflows in Healthcare
abstract: arXiv:2606.28666v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Agent-based AI has enabled the automation of tasks by exposing application tools and resources to large language models (LLMs). However, to improve scope and accuracy, agents are often given access rights that exceed those of ordinary users, introducing significant security risks and potential regulatory breaches. This paper applies the AI Trust, Risk, and Security Management (TRiSM) framework to a medical report-generation application to demonstrate how an insecure baseline workflow can be transformed into a security-conscious agentic workflow. Both designs were evaluated with five LLMs (Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-4.1-nano, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-5.4-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash) across 800 report generations and 500 attack trials covering RAG poisoning, data-field injection and client-side network injection. The redesign reduced attack success from 31% to 10% for RAG poisoning and from 42% to 25% for data-field injection (McNemar p < 0.00

translated_title: 为什么信任你的智能体？TRiSM引导的医疗保健代理工作流带来的实证安全收益
translated_abstract: 基于智能体的AI通过向大语言模型（LLM）开放应用工具和资源，实现了任务自动化。然而，为了提升覆盖范围和准确性，智能体通常被授予超出普通用户的访问权限，这带来了重大安全风险和潜在的监管违规。本文将AI信任、风险与安全管理（TRiSM）框架应用于医疗报告生成应用，展示了如何将不安全的基础工作流转变为具有安全意识的智能体工作流。两种设计均通过五个LLM（Claude Haiku 4.5、GPT-4.1-nano、GPT-4.1-mini、GPT-5.4-mini和Gemini 2.5 Flash）进行了评估，涵盖800次报告生成和500次攻击试验，包括RAG投毒、数据字段注入和客户端网络注入。重新设计使RAG投毒的攻击成功率从31%降至10%，数据字段注入的攻击成功率从42%降至25%（McNemar p < 0.00…
tldr: 本文首次将TRiSM安全框架应用于医疗报告生成的智能体工作流，通过大规模实证评估证明安全导向的重新设计可显著降低RAG投毒和数据字段注入等攻击的成功率。
